pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: The dark regions exhibit sub-polygonal geometries with predominantly smooth, curvilinear boundaries and narrow edge gradients. Patch area is relatively uniform across the mid-flank, transitioning to larger, more vertically elongated geometries on the lower neck area.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: The light-colored negative space forms a continuous interconnected topological graph. Junction nodes are primarily tri-furcated. The pixel thickness of these pathways is consistent, maintaining a narrow and distinct separation between the darker patches.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: The mane silhouette shows a consistent, low-amplitude serrated profile against the sky. The edge is composed of high-frequency, fine-grained peaks corresponding to individual hair groupings.
dorsal_ridge_profile.contour_gaps: Abrupt structural breaks are visible in the mane line where perching birds occlude the continuous edge. A distinct topographical dip is also observed at the junction of the posterior neck and the shoulder ridge.

other_distinctive_markers: Multiple small avian organisms (oxpeckers) are perched along the dorsal ridge of the neck and the posterior flank, creating localized visual occlusions of the giraffe's anatomy.
